meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 8: Security Best Practices (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about MCP's vulnerability reporting process are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Public issues, discussions and pull requests must not be used for security reports
CVEs are issued through GitHub's CNA as part of the GHSA workflow
A crash one stdio peer can cause in the other is always in scope
Reports go through GitHub Security Advisories on the affected repository
Each SDK publishes its fix independently, as soon as it is ready

questions.explanation: Private reporting through GHSA is the channel and CVEs come through GitHub's CNA. stdio peer-only crash, hang or DoS is out of scope because the peers share a trust boundary, unless the same code is reachable remotely or escapes a sandbox. Maintainers coordinate so fixes and advisories ship together.

questions.question: Which values must a server treat as untrusted, even though they arrived over an authenticated connection? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A state handle passed as a tool argument
The server's own serverInfo that it returns in each result
A user identity asserted in a tool argument, such as "I am joe@example.com"
requestState echoed back by the client
The audience claim inside a token the server itself validated

questions.explanation: requestState travelled through the client, a handle is a name rather than a credential, and client-supplied identity can be forged, so identity must come from the verified token (for example the sub claim). A validated aud claim is trustworthy; serverInfo is the server's own self-report and is untrusted by the client, not by the server.

questions.question: Which of these are listed as common scope-design mistakes? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Emitting all scopes needed for one operation in a single challenge
Trusting the scopes in a token without server-side authorization logic
Publishing every possible scope in scopes_supported
Using wildcard or omnibus scopes such as * or full-access
Letting the authorization server issue a subset of the requested scopes

questions.explanation: A, B and C are mistakes. Emitting all scopes for the current operation in one challenge is explicitly recommended over incremental challenges, and down-scoping tolerance, where the AS grants a subset, is also recommended.
